To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Reformation in sixteenth-century Gaelic Ireland was a failure because the reformers were unable to agree among themselves about the nature of their mission and the methods to be employed in its pursuit.

the Reformation in sixteenth-century Irish was a failure because of the lack of a native Protestant leadership and because of the failure of the Protestant leadership to understand and appreciate the nature and extent of the problems that it faced.

there existed within the Reformation a conflict between the two main strands of its thought, that this conflict was rooted in the intellectual history of the Reformers, and that this intellectual conflict had political and social consequences for the movement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
three questions: (1) Why did reformers fail to win the hearts and minds of the native population?
the following questions: 1) What was the intellectual and political context of the Reformation movement in Ireland?
the relationship between the Reformation and the Irish.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Reformation in sixteenth-century Gaelic Ireland was a failure because the Reformation in England was also a failure.
, while the Reformation in England was a political and religious movement, the Reformation in sixteenth-century England was a social movement.
the Reformation in sixteenth-century Gaelic Ireland was not so much a failure as a non-event.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have tried to understand the Reformation as it was experienced by those who were involved in it, and in particular the ways in which it was experienced by the Irish.
the Reformation in sixteenth-century Ulster, as elsewhere in Ireland, was not a movement of the people, but of the elite.
the Reformation failed because the reformers failed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Reformation in England was not the only Reformation.
there was no single reforming party or movement in Ireland, but rather a variety of reforming parties or movements.
the Reformation was a movement which failed to take root in Irish society.
